title: CleanCodeGatesReport
description: Agnostic report emitted by clean-code-gates CLI.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version of this report format.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the report was generated.

baseRef.description: Git base ref; present when kind=diff.

instrument.description: Where the measurement's own settings came from. `.cleancode-gates.json` is deep-merged user-wins and lives inside the tree being measured, so the fields that decide what is measured and how hard — roots, exclude, per-gate exempt and thresholds — are read from the merge-base copy when a base ref is known, and the run happens on those values. Every disagreement with the working tree is listed in `moves`.

anchored.description: False when the run had no base to anchor to (project/module/files scope with no --base-ref); the working-tree config was used and no claim is made about it.

baseRef.description: The ref the instrument was read from; null when anchored is false.

source.description: defaults: the base ref carried no readable config, so the built-in defaults were the anchor — never the working-tree copy.

moves.description: Anchored fields where the working tree disagreed with the anchor. Non-empty is a reviewer finding: the instrument moved inside the change under review.

direction.description: changed: the key is not one whose direction this tool knows, so both values are reported and neither is characterised.

rigor.description: How rigorously this run was verified, and what that changed. Rigor scales the work, never the disclosure: every gate still runs and every finding is still reported — what a lower level changes is whether a finding blocks. Stamped on every report, `hardened` included, so a reader never has to infer the level from a missing line. See docs/adr/0024.

level.description: sketch: it runs, nothing is claimed about quality. delivery: it does what the Acceptance says and the happy path is proven. hardened: plus the gates hold and the mutants die.

source.description: Where the level came from. `config` is the merge-base anchored `.cleancode-gates.json` value; `default` is hardened.

demoted.description: Gate id to number of blockers this level demoted to warnings. The findings themselves are kept, marked `demotedFrom`, and reported.

reportOnly.description: Gates that found blockers this level does not stop on.

skipped.description: Gates this level did not run at all; each carries measurement.state "unmeasured" with reason rigor-<level>.

gatesErrored.description: Gates whose run failed outright, measuring nothing.

tool.description: Tool that ran this gate (builtin, eslint, jest, stryker, etc.).

command.description: Exact command that was run, if applicable.

thresholds.description: Thresholds used for this gate run.

measurement.description: Whether this gate actually measured anything, independent of whether it passed. A consumer asking 'did it pass' reads status; one asking 'was this actually verified' reads measurement.state. Adapters add their own counts (mutants, measured, unrun, excluded, budgetSeconds, ...).

state.description: empty: nothing in scope to measure. measured: the whole scope was measured. partial: some of it was not. unmeasured: the run produced no comparable value at all.

reason.description: Why the measurement is partial or unmeasured, e.g. killed-on-clock, no-report, nothing-ran, mutant-cap, time-budget.

fixHint.description: Actionable fix suggestion for a fixer agent.

baselineGrandfathered.description: True when the finding was pre-existing in the baseline manifest.

demotedFrom.description: Set when the run's rigor level lowered this finding's severity. The finding was found and is reported; it did not stop the run.

rigor.description: The level that demoted this finding. Present only alongside demotedFrom.
